## Overview

My research trajectory is sustained by **continuous competitive funding** as **Principal Investigator (PI)** and as **team member**, and is articulated around two long-term observational infrastructures — the **Gibraltar Fixed Time Series (GIFT)** and the **Balearic Ocean Acidification Time Series (BOATS)** — and the **OCEAN–IA** framework that applies artificial intelligence to environmental impact assessment in marine systems.

## Current Position · MOMENTUM Programme

### MOMENTUM — Postdoctoral Excellence Programme
**Role**: Postdoctoral Researcher · **Period**: 2024 – 2028 · **Funding**: CSIC

Research framed within the **OCEAN–IA** line: development of deep-learning methodologies for reconstructing and predicting ocean acidification, deoxygenation and greenhouse-gas fluxes in coastal and deep-sea environments, integrating high-frequency oceanographic observations, satellite products and geophysical information.

**Main objectives**:

- Deep-learning models (BiLSTM) for continuous pH, pCO₂ and GHG time series
- Integration of oceanographic, meteorological and seismic data
- Extension of the OCEAN–IA framework to polar systems (Deception Island, Antarctica)
- Assessment of ocean acidification trends in the Western Mediterranean

## Projects as Principal Investigator

### GHG Monitoring across Andalusian Ecosystems
**Entity**: ICMAN-CSIC — Grants for Technical & R&D Management Support
**Budget**: **€ 80,000**

Multiplatform monitoring of greenhouse-gas emissions across coastal, continental and marine systems of Andalusia, combining fixed stations, autonomous sensors and ship-based observations.

### INDICLIMA — Key Indicators for Climate-Change Impacts in Deep-Sea Ecosystems
**Period**: July 2024 – July 2027 · **Funding**: EU NextGeneration — BIOACT 2024 · **Budget**: **€ 67,850.10**

Development of biogeochemical indicators for evaluating climate-change impacts on deep-sea ecosystems of the Western Mediterranean, building on the methodological outputs of EVALUARTE.

### EVALUARTE — Vulnerability of Deep-Sea Ecosystems to Climate Change
**Period**: June 2022 – June 2025 · **Funding**: Government of the Balearic Islands — *Vicenç Mut 2022* · **Budget**: **€ 114,000**

Integrated assessment of the vulnerability of deep-sea ecosystems to climate change in the Western Mediterranean, examining the state of the art and trends in the Balearic Sea Basin.

### STARTER — Impact of Wastewater Outfalls on *Posidonia oceanica*
**Period**: March 2021 – March 2022 · **Funding**: Cátedra de la Mar — Fundación Iberostar · **Budget**: **€ 12,000**

Quantification of the impact of wastewater discharges on the ecosystem services provided by *Posidonia oceanica* meadows in Mallorca.

### Margalida Comas 2017 — pH Variability in Coastal Areas
**Period**: December 2017 – December 2019 · **Funding**: Government of the Balearic Islands · **Budget**: **€ 66,000**

Comparison across scales and sources of pH variability in Mediterranean coastal areas, establishing baselines for ocean acidification monitoring. Machine-learning applications for pH reconstruction, published in *Scientific Reports*.

### AAEE111/2017 — Acquisition of Autonomous pH Sensors (SAMI)
**Period**: June 2018 – July 2019 · **Funding**: Government of the Balearic Islands · **Budget**: **€ 19,560**

Acquisition and deployment of autonomous SAMI pH sensors for continuous monitoring of ocean acidification in Mediterranean coastal waters.

> **Total competitive funding captured as PI: € 359,410.10**

## Observational Infrastructures

### GIFT — Gibraltar Fixed Time Series *(2008 – Present)*

Long-term oceanographic series based on high-frequency sampling of biogeochemical and physical variables in the Strait of Gibraltar.
**Role**: *Scientific coordinator*.

- Quantification of decadal acidification rates in Atlantic and Mediterranean water masses
- Results integrated into the **IPCC SROCC (2019)** and the **CLIVAR-Spain 2025** report
- Data deposited in IOC-UNESCO and DIGITAL.CSIC open repositories

### BOATS — Balearic Ocean Acidification Time Series *(2018 – Present)*

Coastal observation network in the Balearic Sea, with emphasis on *Posidonia oceanica* meadows.
**Role**: *Co-founder and co-Principal Investigator*.

- AI-based methodologies for continuous pH reconstruction
- Characterisation of acidification trends, water-column oxygenation and GHG emissions
- Methodologies transferred to deep-sea ecosystems through EVALUARTE and INDICLIMA

### COJOHNS — Johnsons Cove Time Series *(2024 – Present)*

High-frequency time series of seawater **pCO₂** and biogeochemical properties (temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll) in **Johnsons Cove, Livingston Island (South Shetland Islands, Antarctica)** — a glacier-influenced embayment adjacent to a tidewater glacier on the western Antarctic Peninsula.
**Role**: *Scientific coordinator*.

- Continuous **pCO₂ monitoring via a fixed mooring** with an autonomous CO₂ sensor (active since February 2024)
- First year-round record of carbonate-system variability in a glacier-fed Antarctic embayment
- Quantification of air–sea CO₂ fluxes to assess the area as a sink or source of CO₂ to the atmosphere
- Strengthens the observational framework for **coastal carbon inputs to the Southern Ocean** and improves the representation of Antarctic waters in global C-cycle assessments

## Open-Source Tools & Digital Transfer

### [GIFT Dashboard](https://github.com/susafle/GIFT_DASHBOARD)
Open-source platform for managing, visualising and analysing the GIFT biogeochemical time series. Developed as lead author and aligned with the FAIR principles.

### [CO₂ Prediction · BiLSTM](https://github.com/susafle/CO2_prediction_BiLSTM)
Deep-learning model that integrates oceanographic, meteorological and **seismic** data to estimate seawater CO₂ at **Deception Island (Antarctica)**. A novel methodological development identifying the influence of volcanic seismicity on CO₂ dynamics, fully reproducible through open data and open models (published in *Scientific Data*, 2025).

## Research Infrastructure

### Scientific Equipment

Experience with the design, deployment and maintenance of:

- Continuous CO₂ measurement systems (LICOR, Contros HydroC)
- Autonomous pH sensors (SAMI, SeaFET)
- Oxygen, temperature, salinity and fluorescence optodes
- CTD rosettes and oceanographic moorings
- Laboratory instrumentation for carbon-system analysis (DIC/TA coulometry, spectrophotometry, gas chromatography)

The results of my research have contributed to:

- **Regional policy support** — Andalusian Regional Government, Government of the Balearic Islands
